newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP says copper cost 86 cents in US.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP says copper cost 86 cents in US.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, the world's second largest copper producer, said on Tuesday that the cost of production at its U.S. copper mines was running at about US85 cents per pound.
This compared with costs of 40 cents or less a pound at BHP's Escondida mine in Chile and Ok Tedi mine in Papua New Guinea, chairman Brian Loton told the annual meeting.
Loton said that at current international copper prices of around 86 cents a pound, BHP "needed to work very hard" for profits in the U.S. operations.
BHP announced a 23 percent drop in first quarter net profit on Friday. Group net profit for the three months to August 31 was A$287 million, down from A$372 million a year earlier.
Net profit before minorities from BHP's copper division was A$85 million for the August quarter, 55 percent down on the same quarter a year earlier because of lower prices.
BHP estimated the effect of the lower copper prices had adversely impacted profit by A$150 million.
BHP also said on Friday that its Magma Copper Co unit in the U.S. made a loss in the quarter ended August 31. BHP completed its US$2.4 billion takeover of Magma earlier this year.
